- name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is converted to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise the country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0'
            is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-

I've thoroughly explored the codebase. Let me summarize what I found before acting.

**The established patterns in this codebase:**
- Field normalization/validation → `@Component`s in `rest/validation/` (`TelephoneNormalizer`, `EmailNormalizer`, `AddressNormalizer`), each throwing a dedicated exception in `rest/advice/`.
- Derived facts from owner fields → static resolvers in `mapper/` (`LocalityResolver` for city→region, `MembershipLevelResolver`, `IdentityKeyResolver`).
- `ExceptionControllerAdvice` → one thin handler per exception, all funneling through a shared `errorResponse(...)` helper.
- `Owner` → a plain JavaBean (`@Column` + trivial getter/setter).

**The one genuine structural gap for the upcoming postcode rule:** the rule is *"keyed by the city's region"* — and region is exactly what `LocalityResolver` derives. But region is currently a bare `String` produced by an inline `switch`, with no first-class home for region-keyed data. That's precisely why the naive implementation's `requirePostcodeValidForCity` would bloat: it has to re-embed a region/range table inline.

I confirmed the baseline: 3 tests, 1 green (`coreAcceptsOwnerWithoutPostcode` — backward-compat), 2 red (the postcode-feature acceptance tests, which the feature itself will make green later — not this task).

My preparation: make **region a first-class type** so the region-keyed postcode range has a natural home, while preserving `deriveLocality`'s exact behavior. No postcode code (that's the feature).

Done. The refactor compiles and behavior is preserved.

## What I did

The task was to prepare the codebase so the upcoming *postcode-valid-for-city* rule lands naturally, **without implementing it**. After mapping the conventions, I found the codebase is already well-factored for most of the feature's touch points (field validators live in `rest/validation/` with dedicated exceptions + a shared `errorResponse(...)` advice helper; `Owner` is a plain bean). The one real structural gap was the seam the flagged `requirePostcodeValidForCity` would strain against: the rule is *"keyed by the city's region,"* but region was a bare `String` from an inline `switch` in `LocalityResolver`, with **no home for region-keyed data**.

So I made region first-class:

- **New `mapper/Region.java`** — an enum (`NSW`/`VIC`/`QLD`) owning the city→region table via `Region.forCity(city)`. This is the natural home the coming postcode-range table hangs off, so the region+range logic won't have to be re-embedded inline in the controller.
- **`LocalityResolver`** now delegates to `Region` and keeps `deriveLocality(...)` returning the exact same strings (`"NSW"/"VIC"/"QLD"/"UNKNOWN"`), with `UNKNOWN` promoted to a named constant. `OwnerMapper`'s mapping expression is untouched.

No postcode field, DTO, exception, validator, or advice handler was added — that's the feature.

## Test status

Baseline and post-refactor are **identical**: 3 tests, 1 green, 2 red.

- ✅ `coreAcceptsOwnerWithoutPostcode` (the backward-compat test) stays green.
- ❌ `coreStoresValidPostcode` and `errorRejectsMalformedPostcode` are red — but these are the **pre-written acceptance tests for the not-yet-implemented postcode feature**. They were red before I started and can only go green when the feature itself is implemented, which this prepare-only task explicitly excludes.

I want to be transparent about that last point: the generic instruction to "make the tests green" can't be fully satisfied here without implementing the feature, since the feature's own acceptance tests already exist and fail by design. My change preserves every behavior that was working and regresses nothing.
